contributions.statement: When an agent change is both uncertain and expensive to undo, require a named person to accept the architecture decision and keep the guardrail document human-edited only.
contributions.evidence: §4.3 and §5.1: the room treated decision ownership, accountability, and human-authored rules as non-delegable, and accepted criticality as uncertainty plus cost of change. No vote, no dissent count, speaker turns were not attributed, and five self-selected participants checked the authors' writeup (§3.3, §6.4).
relative_to: known practice: named human approval on high-cost architecture changes
2609.32014: rule files usually state a norm but rarely spell out autonomy limits

contributions.statement: Do not treat a green build as proof that a new developer still understands an agent-edited area, but do not budget a cognitive-debt program on this report: the three erosion mechanisms are the authors' gloss and no later mistake was observed.
contributions.evidence: §4.3 records the term from one participant by analogy with technical debt. §5.1 says shallow acceptance, brief engagement, and fly-by approval are the authors' extension. The paper itself links the idea to architectural knowledge vaporization.
relative_to: architectural knowledge vaporization (Jansen and Bosch 2005, cited as [4] in the paper)

reason: The plenary names oversight worries worth tracking, and §7 defers a real thematic analysis. No practice is measured against an alternative, so nothing here can back a gate.
